paragraphs: Rav Beruna said in the name of Rav: Shabbat 21a, 24b, 26a. He and his colleague Rav Chananel were students of Rav (Pesachim 103, end of side a); Rav Yeiva the Elder was attending them. Yevamot 110a. Rav Tavla said: Rav Beruna said in the name of Rav (see his entry). Rav Beruna was sitting and reporting a teaching that Shmuel had said. Rabbi Elazar of the house of Rav said to him, “Did Shmuel say this?” He answered, “Yes.” He said, “Show me Shmuel’s lodging.” He showed it to him, and he asked Shmuel, “Did the master say this?” Eruvin 74a. Rabbi Eliezer of the house of Rav said to him, “Did Rav say this?” He answered, “Yes.” He said, “Show me Rav’s house,” and said to him, “Did the master say this?” (There, 85b.) Rabbi Elazar—another reading: Rabbi Ilai—said to Ulla, “When you go up there, inquire after the welfare of Rav Beruna, my brother, for he is a great man and rejoices in commandments”: Berakhot 9b. Perhaps he is his brother, or his friend whom he called “my brother.” Rav Yehudah permitted Rabbi Beruna to sell wine: Avodah Zarah 11b. Rav Beruna raised a contradiction before Rav Yehudah at the winepress of the house of bar Chanina: “Did Shmuel say …?” Eruvin 60a.
